signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: AUD/CHF is the primary G10 expression this week as the Australian Dollar outperforms its peers by an average of +1.407% while the Swiss Franc lags the basket at -0.559%. This 1.967% leader-to-laggard spread is supported by a significant +435bp nominal carry advantage for AUD and a restrictive +0.85% real rate vs CHF's accommodative -0.40%. COT data confirms the trend is backed by institutional demand, with AUD LF net long at +49,749 (pctl 94) following a massive +29,228 4W build. Despite the extreme retail short at 94%, the alignment of carry and spec flow suggests the path of least resistance remains higher. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/CHF; carry advantage and institutional flow support the bilateral divergence. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep for regional sentiment. Risk: Sharp risk-off reversal spikes VIX above 25, triggering a rapid unwind of the high-carry AUD/CHF cross.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.55, holding above its SMA20/200 cluster at 158.75/158.38 despite the Yen's 5-day decline. BoJ holds at 1.0%. This strong put skew contradicts the crowded spec short positioning (JPY LF net -73,641, pctl 12), suggesting institutional players are hedging for a potential BoJ policy shift or intervention near 160.00. Government officials' travel to the US and Switzerland from August 30 adds a layer of diplomatic monitoring to the price action. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; carry-supportive while below the 160.00 intervention threshold. Catalyst: Fed Chair Warsh at Jackson Hole today. Risk: BoJ board members signal a definitive hike bias for the 18 Sep meeting, triggering a short-squeeze.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Volatility Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD is trading at 1.3586, maintaining a position above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3537/1.3418/1.3437) despite a negative Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of -9.3. The options market is pricing in significant tail-risk, with ATM Implied Volatility at 11.0% vs a 30-day Realized Volatility of only 4.8%. This +6.2% Volatility Risk Premium (VRP) indicates the highest protection-buying demand in the G10 space ahead of today's Jackson Hole headlines. COT data shows specs remain heavily net long +46,070 (pctl 92), leaving the pair vulnerable to a long-unwind if the Fed delivers a hawkish surprise. Trade bias: Neutral/range GBP/USD; high vol premium makes directional bets expensive. Catalyst: Fed Chair Warsh speech today. Risk: US data continues to disappoint, forcing a USD-driven move through 1.3650 resistance.

signals.title: USD/NOK — Retail Extreme vs ESI
signals.text: USD/NOK retail sentiment has hit an absolute extreme with 100% community long positioning on Myfxbook. This retail bias directly contradicts the underlying fundamental momentum, where the Norway Economic Surprise Index (ESI) is at a G10-leading +84.0 following sustained data beats. The technical picture reinforces NOK strength, with USD/NOK trading at 9.319 and positioned below its entire SMA20/50/200 stack (9.428/9.610/9.653). While oil prices are slightly lower at $83.0, the prospects of renewed US-Iran tensions and a restrictive +1.15% NOK real rate support further downside for the pair. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK; contrarian to the 100% retail long extreme and supported by data outperformance. Catalyst: Next Norges Bank meeting 24 Sep. Risk: A sharp collapse in WTI oil prices below $75.0 invalidates the NOK strength thesis.
